Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticTurnScheduler

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticTurnScheduler
public final class AgenticTurnScheduler extends Object
Schedules the next step of an agentic scope, unless one is already waiting to run.

A step is one model call (CIB7-2148). It is scheduled when the scope is entered, when a child ends or is removed, and by a step whose model called tools and has not answered yet.

  • Method Details

    • scheduleTurn

      public static void scheduleTurn(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      Inserts a step job for scopeExecution unless one is already waiting.

      Waiting means not yet started and not the job running now: not taken by an executor, or taken by the one that runs this command and still in its queue. Three children ending at once fire three times and mean one thing, there is something new to look at, and the waiting job sees all three because it reads the state rather than the signal. A job that is running does not count: it may have read the state before this change, and skipping here would lose the change for good. The worst that follows is one step more: a job another thread or node has taken but not started yet may still read the change, and the job inserted here then finds nothing new. When the taken one ends the turn, that is a turn of its own, which counts against maxTurns and costs a model call. A job in this thread's own queue is not such a case: a step that starts an asynchronous tool creates the tool's job and the next step, both come in one queue, as the hint or as one acquisition, and the next step runs after the tool has ended.

      The scope's own jobs are read from the execution, which also holds the ones inserted earlier in this transaction -- a database query would not see them, and a step whose tool ended synchronously would schedule twice. Such a job is waiting whatever its lock says: inside the job executor, an exclusive job that a job of the same process instance creates is locked at once, as the hint that this thread runs it next (JobManager.hintJobExecutor).

      A waiting job that was there before is relied upon, so its revision is raised: should it be running after all -- without a lock, through executeJob; past its lock; or taken by an executor after it was read here -- it read the state before this change, and it fails on its own job instead of committing over it, and runs again. Nothing else need collide with a step that only answers.

    • isQueuedOnThisThread

      protected static boolean isQueuedOnThisThread(JobEntity job)
      In the queue of the job executor thread that runs this command: taken, but started only after this command commits, so it reads this change. The executor locks the jobs of its queue before it runs them -- the one a job of the same instance creates, as the hint, and every job of an acquired batch -- so their lock does not tell them from a running job.
